text:
Aria: quick heads up — we're seeing a cluster of structured-output rejects coming from the 'note-gen' route after the strict-validator canary went live (up ~3% reject rate since 00:45 UTC).
Ben: reject rate is small but spike looks correlated with the rollout window. are these hard schema rejects or soft degrade?
Aria: hard schema rejects (validator returns 422). payloads mostly have `attachments: []` instead of the required `attachments: {}` union. some models return empty array now/w/ newer decoder behavior.
Carmen: ugh, that union change surfaced again. do we charge the customer when we reject? last time billing confusion caused a support ticket.
Mike: currently a schema reject still consumes a normal request token budget (we bill on inference attempt) but we tag route as `fncall:rejected`. billing team said we should make that clearer in Console.
Sofia: From UX side, customers interpreted "rejected" as not billed. we need a Console annotation AND an API flag in responses so SDKs can surface it.
Aria: propose steps: 1) temporary routing fallback to permissive-validator for canary slice; 2) add a sampled debug trace for rejected payloads (redact PII) upstream to help model teams; 3) console badge + billing note. thoughts?
Ben: Agree. For (1) can we flip on permissive mode only for the canary tag? We should keep strict for default prod.
Carmen: yes, we have routing policy tokens for slices. config snippet: 
```yaml
routes:
  - name: note-gen
    canary: true
    validator_mode: permissive  # overrides global strictness for canary
```
Ben: Perfect. For (2) telemetry: add `validation.reason` tag and store a 1-per-100 sample (to avoid volume). ops-bot: can you create a metric?
ops-bot: new metric request received: `fncall.validation.rejects.sampled`. Sampling rate default set to 1/100. Reply with :white_check_mark: when done.
ops-bot: metric `fncall.validation.rejects.sampled` created and routed to metrics.ingest.redwood.
Mike: For console, propose a small change: per-route header that shows "validator: strict | permissive" and a line item "last 24h schema rejects (sampled): X" with an explainer tooltip linking to billing. UX mock: /screenshots/??
Sofia: I'll sketch the mock and add the billing copy: "Schema rejects are counted as requests; we sample debug payloads for diagnostics. To avoid unexpected charges, test routes in permissive mode before enabling strict validator."
Aria: One tricky bit: some rejects are downstream adapter coercion — we should annotate `validation.scope` = {model|adapter|hook} so model teams can triage faster. Ben, can tracing add that tag?
Ben: yes, we can propagate the scope. We'll also include `validator.version` and `validation.sampling_id` so we can tie samples back to the exact canary slice.
Carmen: do we want an automatic rollback if rejects exceed threshold for the canary? E.g., 1% reject over 10m?
Mike: We already have a rollout hook but it's opt-in. I think we should enable a conservative auto-backoff for strict-validator canaries: fail-stop + notify on >1% rejects.
Sofia: For notifications, add a Console banner and also post to #release-war-room with a compact payload: route, slice, reject_rate, sample_link.
Aria: I'll open a PR that does: routing override, adds the sampling metric, and registers the console badge. PR will include the config snippet and a dashboard query.
Ben: dashboard query suggestion (Grafana/Prometheus style): 
```promql
sum(rate(fncall_validation_rejects_total{route="note-gen",slice="canary"}[5m]))
/ sum(rate(fncall_requests_total{route="note-gen",slice="canary"}[5m]))
```
Sofia: Add a second panel for sampled payload count and a link that pops up the redacted sample store.
Carmen: timeline? we should ship the permissive fallback ASAP, sampling + metrics next, console UX in follow-up.
Aria: plan: permissive fallback roll -> 10m monitor -> flip back to strict if stable. I'll tag @Ben @Sofia in the PR.
Ben: I'll implement the scope tagging in trace propagation and add the sampling_id.
Mike: ops: make sure the billing team is pinged before we update customer-facing copy.
Sofia: will coordinate with billing and design.
Aria: thanks — if anyone sees additional reject patterns, drop examples here. :pray:
Carmen: small nit — we should log the validator schema version in the rejection reason so we can bisect schema changes.
Ben: yep, adding `validator_schema_sha` to the tag.
ops-bot: alerting rule created: `fncall.validation.reject_rate > 0.01 for 10m (canary)` -> post to #release-war-room and page on critical.
Aria: awesome. PR soon.
Sofia: mock uploaded to the design folder. link: https://intranet.redwood.design/note-gen-validator-mock
Ben: thanks all, rolling the permissive override now.
ops-bot: deploy job started for routing changes (job 8921).
ops-bot: deploy job 8921 succeeded in eu-west-1 and us-west-2.
Aria: monitoring — reject rate dropping to baseline. closing the canary incident once we confirm 30m stability.
Carmen: moving the billing copy to docs PR.
Mike: follow-up: we should add an SDK error code `VALIDATION_REJECTED` so downstream apps can treat it explicitly.
Sofia: noted for SDK owners.
Aria: end."
